notes.title: Servants in the land
notes.body: The prayer ends not with political independence but with the community acknowledging Persian imperial domination within the land it regards as ancestral.

verses.restored: And it yieldeth much increase to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins: also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage but remains explicitly pending the later deep Hebrew/source-witness continuity audit. KJV is retained only as the familiar comparison layer.
safety_note: The prayer interprets history theologically from within the returned community. Conquest, enemy destruction, inherited guilt, and foreign domination must not be turned into modern authorization for collective punishment, ethnic supremacy, or war.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare restored wording directly with WLC/OSHB and relevant textual witnesses during the global continuity audit.
